answer: Downregulation of genes primarily drives the metabolic effects of CBD in CRC cells. In the primary comparison (CBD_IC50 vs DMSO; DESeq2-style NB GLM + Wald, padj<0.05, |log2FC|>0.5) 4052 genes are down-regulated vs 3493 up-regulated (down:up = 1.16:1); the down-bias is strongest among moderate-effect genes (|log2FC| 0.5-2: 3115 down vs 2400 up) and at higher expression levels (baseMean>100: 127 down vs 72 up), i.e. among the genes most likely to represent stable metabolic transcript changes. The serum-starvation context confirms the same direction (CBD_IC50_SS vs DMSO_SS: 5525 down vs 3643 up; moderate window 4096 vs 2855). Only near-on/off low-count genes (|log2FC|>4, median baseMean<1) are slightly enriched in the up direction (down: up = 460 vs 797, i.e. 797 up vs 460 down), reflecting dropout-dominated extremes, and the overall majority of significant transcripts is still down-regulated. LIMITATION: GO Biological Process enrichment could not be computed because the offline environment contains no GO annotation and no Ensembl-to-SYMBOL/ENTREZ mapping (verified by filesystem search; no R/Bioconductor, no network); 'primarily drives' is therefore concluded from the direction of differentially expressed transcripts (fully computable DE metrics), not from GO:BP term enrichment.
